rules.statement: In a test project, don't report `null!` when it passes a deliberate null to the code under test to prove the `ArgumentNullException` guard of a non-nullable parameter.
rules.why: The testing conventions allow this one use of the null-forgiving operator; the maintainer declined the finding on that basis.
rules.check: Before flagging `null!` in a test, see whether it is an argument to the member under test in a test that asserts `ArgumentNullException`; flag only other uses, such as dereferencing a captured local or result.

rules.statement: Don't ask for a stored tenant-supplied credential (access key, client secret, key file) to reach a tenant's cloud KMS key; access goes through the provider's recommended identity delegation, such as STS AssumeRole with an external ID, service account impersonation or a consented multi-tenant application.
rules.why: Delegation gives the same reach without a long-lived secret to protect, rotate or leak; a stored-credential option was considered and rejected.
rules.check: Look for new code or review suggestions that persist cloud credentials for tenant key access instead of assuming a granted identity.

rules.statement: Put a policy that must wrap every call (such as confirm-on-success / release-on-failure of a cached client) in one shared, tested type that runs the operation, instead of repeating the try/catch at each call site.
rules.why: A repeated policy has to be changed at every site, and a site that forgets it leaves a broken entry cached or evicts a working one with nothing enforcing it.
rules.check: Look for the same try/catch-with-side-effects pattern copied across several adapters or call sites.

rules.statement: Apply `[ExcludeFromCodeCoverage]` only to pure passthrough code such as SDK construction and delegation; move real behavior (caching, eviction, state tracking) out of an excluded class into a tested type.
rules.why: Logic inside an excluded class is invisible to coverage, so its bugs would not show up in tests.
rules.check: For a class marked `[ExcludeFromCodeCoverage]`, see whether the diff adds branching, caching or state logic to it.

rules.statement: Dispose a disposable client or credential that a cache drops, whether it lost a creation race or was evicted or released, and don't dispose it while a call is still using it.
rules.why: Dropped clients that own channels, HTTP clients or refreshing credentials otherwise hold sockets until finalization, and repeated retries can exhaust connections.
rules.check: Look at `GetOrAdd` races, `TryRemove`, eviction and release paths on caches of disposable objects and check that the removed or losing instance is disposed safely.

rules.statement: Bound a cache whose keys come from tenant- or caller-controlled values, for example with idle expiry that disposes entries, instead of letting it grow for the process lifetime.
rules.why: Memory, connection pools and background refreshes otherwise grow with the number of distinct keys ever used, and tenants control that number.
rules.check: Look for long-lived dictionaries or caches keyed by tenant identities or input values that are only cleared on Dispose.

rules.statement: Don't let a cached lazy creation cache a failure: a `Lazy<T>` whose factory can fail transiently uses `LazyThreadSafetyMode.PublicationOnly`, or a failed creation removes its cache entry.
rules.why: The default `ExecutionAndPublication` mode caches the exception, so the entry stays broken until restart.
rules.check: Look for `Lazy<T>` or cache entries created with the default mode around factories that can throw, especially when the throw happens outside the caller's recovery path.

rules.statement: Put a selection rule that several packages need (such as first-translator-wins over registered handlers) in one public helper, such as an extension method next to the interface, and use it at every call site.
rules.why: Copies of the loop in different packages can drift apart.
rules.check: Look for the same loop over a set of services duplicated in another package or a private helper.

rules.statement: Make `<exception>` doc entries name the exception types actually thrown, with one entry per type, and don't let the cref contradict the text.
rules.why: A caller that catches the documented type can miss the exception actually thrown.
rules.check: Compare `<exception cref>` entries with the prose and with the exceptions the member or the platform calls it makes can throw.

rules.statement: When an event or record is built at several call sites from the same source object, have it take that object (or use a shared factory) instead of copying fields by hand at each site.
rules.why: A call site can forget a field and write incomplete records, such as audit entries without a new field.
rules.check: Look for a new field copied by hand onto the same type at several call sites.

rules.statement: Declare an optional member of a public record as a nullable `{ get; init; }` property, not a positional constructor parameter, consistent with sibling types.
rules.why: Positional optional parameters force callers to pass explicit nulls, and each later optional field breaks call sites.
rules.check: Look for nullable or optional positional parameters added to public records.

rules.statement: In an edit form for an existing resource, prefill every stored field that the submission sends, so that changing one field doesn't silently clear the others.
rules.why: A missing prefill sent the request with no identity, silently moving the key to a different identity.
rules.check: Compare a dialog's initial values with the fields of its submitted request body and the stored resource.

rules.statement: In a test project, merge near-identical setup helpers into one helper with defaulted parameters instead of adding an overload that differs only in a matcher.
rules.why: Two near-identical helpers invite stubbing the wrong one or fixing only one.
rules.check: Look for new test helper overloads that duplicate an existing helper's body.
